stories.question: Which genes change in the endometrial organoids when we add IL-1B on top of estradiol?

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples.
why.pipelines: Bulk human organoid RNA-seq with a real treatment contrast in CEL.Treatment. The atlas's own rnaseq-vs-differentialabundance entry says "If you have no counts yet, both are needed in sequence", so naming both is following the payload, not hedging: acceptable_sets allows either answer.

stories.question: Which genes are turned up or down in the mesenchymal MDA-MB-231 cells compared with the epithelial-like ones?

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples.
why.pipelines: Bulk human cell-line RNA-seq, two subtypes in CEL.Type. Reworded after the first run: the original asked what differs "at the transcript level", which is standard wording for isoform-level analysis, and the model answered rnasplice 3/3. That reading was defensible, so the question was at fault, not the answer. It now names gene-level up/down explicitly.

stories.question: Do the COL2A1-edited chondronoids use different isoforms from the wild type ones?

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples.
why.pipelines: THE library-prep test. DNA.LibraryPrepProtocol says oligo(dT)-primed UMI-based 3' RNA-Seq: only the 3' end is sequenced, so isoform usage is not recoverable. Nothing in the sample-type fields says this — it is only in the prep text.

stories.question: Compare the infected and the uninfected animals for me.

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples.
why.pipelines: Deliberately vague -- "compare the infected and the uninfected animals" names no measurement. On bulk mouse RNA both a gene-level and an isoform-level reading are legitimate, which is what the ambiguous class is for; the earlier singleton expectation contradicted its own class.

stories.question: Do any of these produce a PCA and a sample-distance heatmap as part of the standard output, or would I have to make those myself?

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples.
why.pipelines: rnaseq emits both from its DESeq2 QC step. That fact lives in the output guide and in no metadata field -- and it is the one the model missed when the docs were withheld earlier.

why.pipelines: rnavar is the only atlas entry that emits variant calls. It is NOT one of the pipelines whose docs are fetched, so this is answerable from atlas prose alone -- a useful contrast with the cases that need the docs.

stories.question: Can I get PSI values for exon skipping out of these chondronoids?

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples.
why.pipelines: The output framing of sho-3prime-isoforms. A 3'DGE library sequences only the 3' end, so no PSI is recoverable however the request is phrased. Pairs with qout-psi-events: same deliverable, different library, opposite answer.
